System Architecture

SupplyLens is structured as three semi-independent organs. Each runs on its own schedule and communicates through well-defined interfaces. The mouth ingests continuously. The gut processes whenever raw data arrives. The presentation layer reads Neo4j on demand, independently of when either of the others last ran.

Color key: green = confirmed working · orange = service up, integration incomplete · red = not yet built/deployed

Organ 1 — The Mouth (Ingestion)

The mouth runs on its own schedule. It does not parse, infer, or score — it only collects and stores raw material. Three trigger paths feed into a common MongoDB store.

Mouth I/O:

Direction Item Format
In Company name / SKU / barcode Plain text
In Cron schedule Time trigger (n8n)
In Researcher-provided URLs Plain text
Out Scraped HTML pages UTF-8 string + {source_url, timestamp, sha256}
Out Downloaded PDFs / XLS / DOC Binary + {filename, sha256, mime_type}
Out Trade flow records JSON — {hs_code, reporter, partner, value, year}
Out Bill-of-lading records JSON — {shipper, consignee, goods_description, port}
Out Facility records JSON — {name, lat, lon, country, certifications[]}
Out News/violation events JSON — {actor, location, event_type, date, url}
Out Company ownership records JSON — {lei, name, parent_lei, subsidiaries[]}
Store All outputs MongoDB CT121 — collection raw_scrapes

Organ 2 — The Gut (Processing & Inference)

The gut is triggered by new documents arriving in MongoDB. It loops through extraction, embedding, inference, scoring, and graph writing until no new nodes are found or the depth limit is reached.

Gut I/O:

Direction Item Format
In Raw HTML UTF-8 string — multipart POST to Unstructured CT117
In Binary documents (PDF/XLS/DOC) Binary — PUT to Tika CT115
In Structured JSON (trade/facility/news) JSON — parsed directly by LangGraph
Out Text elements JSON array — [{text, type, metadata}] from Unstructured
Out 768-dim embeddings float[] — nomic-embed-text via LiteLLM, upserted to Qdrant
Out Inferred relationships JSON array — [{name, country, tier, supplies, confidence}]
Out Supplier / RawMaterial nodes Neo4j MERGE — {name, country, tier, confidence, inferred, signals[]}
Out SUPPLIED_BY / SOURCED_FROM edges Neo4j MERGE — {confidence, inferred: true, source}
Out EvidenceClaim nodes Neo4j MERGE — {source_url, sha256, timestamp, method_version}
Store Nodes + edges + evidence Neo4j CT114 + Qdrant CT102 (embeddings)

Organ 3 — The Presentation Layer

The presentation layer reads Neo4j on demand. Three independent interfaces serve three research use cases: geographic visualization, graph topology exploration, and regulatory report generation.

Presentation I/O:

Direction Item Format
In Supply chain graph Cypher query results from Neo4j CT114
In Semantic search results Qdrant similarity query — top-k chunks
Out Geographic arc map Browser UI — Kepler.gl: nodes + arcs + evidence panel
Out Graph topology view Browser UI — NeoDash CT130 / Neo4j Bloom
Out SQL analytics dashboard Browser UI — Superset CT206 / Metabase CT202
Out EDRM regulatory report PDF — every claim hashed and traceable
Out BPMN process export XML — bpmn.io format for regulatory submission

Infrastructure Map

Data flows top to bottom through three organ layers. All IPs are listed in the Services chapter.

Signal to Action — End-to-End Data Flow

A researcher submits a company name or product SKU. The mouth resolves the identity through GS1 and OpenCorporates, builds a list of URLs to scrape, and stores raw HTML and downloaded documents in MongoDB. That write triggers the gut: LangGraph orchestrates text extraction (Unstructured for HTML/PDF, Tika for binary formats), embedding into Qdrant, and LLM inference of probable supplier relationships. Each inferred node is scored using a weighted fusion of five OSINT signal types and written into Neo4j with a full evidence stamp — source URL, SHA-256 hash, inference method version, and confidence score. The loop repeats, following newly discovered nodes, until the depth limit is reached or no new nodes emerge.

From Neo4j, the presentation layer consumes the graph on demand. NeoDash renders supplier counts, tier breakdowns, and risk heatmaps. The evidence map plots confirmed and inferred suppliers as geographic arcs. A researcher reviewing a flagged node can pull the full EDRM package for that node — every source document, its hash, the signal weights that produced the confidence score, and any violations detected — and use it as the basis for a regulatory report submitted to a national competent authority or the European Commission.
